title.narrative: Results Indicator 10. Share of electricity auctions for regulated customers in which non-conventional renewable energy participate.

comment.narrative: The indicator has not made progress to date since the draft regulation on supply contracts for regulated users has not yet been approved, and therefore non-conventional renewable energies cannot yet participate in electricity supply auctions for regulated customers. Currently, there is a higher percentage share of generation sources that use renewable resources; However, the plants of this type that entered in recent years have been developed by private initiative and as a result of electricity auctions for regulated customers. It will be possible to know when electricity auctions will be held for regulated users, when the distribution companies communicate their bidding programs, which will occur once the aforementioned Regulation has been approved and Osinergmin publishes the corresponding procedure.

title.narrative: Results Indicator 8. Number of housing units from Fondo MiVivienda registered in the National Registry of Sustainable Buildings and Urban Developments.

comment.narrative: The indicator has not shown progress to date due to several factors: (i) the Technical Code of Sustainable Construction 2021 (CT) came into effect on July 23, 2023—one year later than initially anticipated in its approval decree (July 2022); (ii) housing projects require longer formulation and execution times than the period since the CT's implementation; and (iii) the registration platform was only recently created and launched in September 2024, with no projects yet registered. Nevertheless, the MiVivienda Fund has confirmed that with the usual pipeline of projects the goal is still expected to be met by the project's closure.

title.narrative: Results Indicator 5. Number of people living in areas with local EOCs operating according to new guidelines.

comment.narrative: Due to extensive dissemination and technical assistance by the Institute, the goal has been exceeded. A total of 99 existing EOCs have been updated according to the new guidelines, benefiting 6,961,651 people, while 297 new EOCs have been established from 2022 to 2025, benefiting 3,131,469 people, all in compliance with the new guidelines. Each updated EOC has a specific resolution, which is properly stored in the database. The new guidelines focus on improving the management of information related to events and emergencies in the territories, leading to a higher number of reports being recorded in the National Disaster Information System (SINPAD).

comment.narrative: By the end of 2025, a total of 12.4 million people live in cities or settlements populated with urban planning instruments that integrate disaster risk management and public space management, in accordance with the main objectives and guidelines established by the National Housing and Urban Planning Policy for 2030 and the DUS Law. title.narrative: Results Indicator 9. Reduction of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and local pollutants (PM2.5, SO2 and Nox) linked to the implementation of scrapping programs, Law No. 31596 and the PLANMET 2040 (Strat

target.value: 281,240 MtCO2e per year 1,952 Mt of local pollutants per year

comment.narrative: The indicator includes the scrapping of 1,000 vehicles under the Ministry of Transport (MTC) program and 6,848 vehicles by the Urban Transport Authority for Lima and Callao (ATU). As of October 2024, the ATU has scrapped 107 vehicles, while the MTC has yet to launch its scrapping program. The scrapping of these 107 vehicles by the ATU has resulted in an estimated reduction of 13,892.4 tons/year of greenhouse gas (CO2) emissions and 207.3 tons/year of local pollutants. The ATU projects that an additional 150 vehicles could be scrapped by the end of 2024. MTC and ATU agreed to prepare a contingency plan to address the bottlenecks and thus achieve the proposed target.

actual.value: 13,892.4 MtCO2e/year of CO2 and 207.3 tn/year of local pollutants

title.narrative: Results Indicator 1. Allocation reports are prepared and published, in line with Peru's sustainable bond framework.

comment.narrative: In October 2021, Peru issued its first Sustainable Bond, comprising US$2.25 billion in 12-year bonds and US$1 billion in 50-year bonds, in line with its Sustainable Bond Framework. Additionally, Peru issued a €1 billion social bond aimed at European investors, maturing in November 2036. In May 2023, Peru issued its first sustainable sovereign bond in local currency, valued at approximately $2.5 billion. In total, about $6.75 billion has been raised through four sustainable bonds. The Allocation and Impact Report for the 2021 Social Bond and Sustainable Bonds was published on November 15, 2022, and the Allocation and Impact Report for Peru's 2023 Sustainable Bond was released on June 28, 2024. With the publication of these two reports, the goal of Result Indicator 1 has been met.

title.narrative: Results Indicator 4. Percentage of detailed Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs) and EIA modifications that are evaluated within the timeframe established by the regulatory framework (%).

comment.narrative: The updated Procedimiento Único del Proceso de Certificación Ambiental took effect on January 1, 2025, but projects that started earlier are not subject to it, so few processes have been fully completed under the new regulation. Its impact on this PA's indicator is expected to become evident toward the end of 2026. The rule allowing technical opinions from the Sistema Nacional de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental to use a list of specialists has been implemented gradually. While some technical reviewers completed approval between 2023-2024, not all are hiring technical reviewers due to budget constraints. The recent increase in the PA indicator is attributed to closer coordination of the Servicio Nacional de Certificación Ambiental para las Inversiones Sostenibles (SENACE) with consulting firms, and sector-based focus groups to increase quality of environmental impact assessments and monitoring efforts. SENACE also noted concerns about sustaining this approach given current budget cuts.

title.narrative: Results Indicator 4. Percentage of detailed Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs) and EIA modifications that are evaluated within the timeframe established by the regulatory framework (%).

comment.narrative: While Legislative Decree No. 1570 is currently being implemented, MINAM/SENACE have not yet provided data – following the established methodology - to report progress in meeting target. SENACE identified several factors hindering progress towards the results target, including: (a) budget limitations for both SENACE and the OTs; (b) low-quality studies leading to a significant number of revisions; and (c) OTs failing to meet review deadlines as per the standards. However, SENACE anticipates improvements based on: (a) ongoing coordination to secure increased budgets for both SENACE and the OTs; (b) full implementation of payrolls across all involved OTs; (c) enforcement of recently approved regulations aimed at expediting review times, such as DS 004-2024-MINAM and DS 002-2024-Ministry of Environment (MINAM); and (d) the approval of the updated Unique Environmental Certification Process (PUPCA), scheduled for January 2025.

title.narrative: Results Indicator 6. Share of priority communities that have prepared community risk maps in consultation with women's social organizations and have made them publicly available.

comment.narrative: By the end of 2024, 332 communities are reported to have already prepared the maps, exceeding the established goal. It was also reported that, in accordance with DS No. 060-2024-PCM, these activities must henceforth be articulated to the Community Education Plan at the provincial level, in order to ensure sustainability. This implies that the Instituto Nacional de Defensa Civil ceases to directly lead the execution of community programs and assumes a role of advice and technical accompaniment, while implementation passes to regional and local governments, with execution through district municipalities. Governments will develop their own community education plans and officials will have to be certified in their competencies
